messages:
customer_jane: Hi — we're seeing intermittent 401s in the Console when trying to connect to /v1/generate. Happens ~1/20 requests. No app code changes. Request ID in the response header is sometimes missing. Can you advise on what to collect?
maya.k: sorry you're hitting this. can you grab a HAR+console logs from the browser and the response headers for one of the failed requests? ideally a cURL too. i'll share step-by-step.
aj: short checklist: reproduce in incognito -> open DevTools -> "Preserve log" -> Reproduce -> Right click -> Save as HAR with content. also copy the failed request -> Copy -> Copy as cURL.
leo: include the network request headers/response headers (esp x-request-id / x-rw-request-id) and the server time in the response. if request id is missing, capture the full response body.
maya.k: full step-by-step (Chrome / Edge):
- Open an incognito window (helps remove extensions).
- Cmd+Opt+I / F12 -> Network tab. Check "Preserve log".
- Reproduce the failure.
- Right‑click on the top-level entry -> Save all as HAR with content (this includes bodies).
- Switch to Console tab -> Right‑click -> Save as -> copy console output to a .txt (or screenshot).
- Find the failed request in Network -> Right click -> Copy -> Copy as cURL (bash). paste that into a .txt as well.
- If possible, click the failed request -> Headers -> look for any x-request-id / x-rw-request-id / x-trace-id and note them.
aj: Firefox quick notes (if user on FF):
- DevTools -> Network -> use "Persist Logs" -> reproduce -> right click -> Save all as HAR.
- Console -> Export visible messages via context menu.
leo: when saving HAR, set file name like: companyname-<date>-<incident>-har.zip or .har. we prefer a single zip with: network.har, console.txt, curl.txt, repro-steps.txt
maya.k: security note: please redact any Authorization or API keys before uploading. if you can't remove them, upload to our secure intake (link below) and mark it restricted. do NOT paste raw api keys in the thread.
support-bot: Upload link: https://uploads.redwood.ai/support (expiring link) :lock:
customer_jane: thanks — attaching HAR now. one more issue: the UI shows a CORS-like error in console even though server returns 200 for some.
aj: if you see a CORS error while the server response is 200, check for an OPTIONS preflight failing or mismatched Access-Control-Allow-Origin. in the HAR you'll see the OPTIONS entry.
leo: also run a curl repro from your machine so we can compare server behaviour without browser interference. from the cURL we requested earlier, run: curl -i 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' --data-binary @payload.json and paste output.
maya.k: example repro-steps.txt to include with upload:
- Browser: Chrome 112.0.XXXX, OS: macOS 13.6
- Time window: 2026-03-16T14:10:00Z to 2026-03-16T14:16:00Z
- Affected path: /v1/generate
- Frequency: 1/20 requests -> 401 or blank response headers
- Actions to reproduce: Click "Generate" twice quickly, repeat ~8 times
- Files attached: network.har, console.txt, curl.txt
customer_jane: uploaded at https://uploads.redwood.ai/support/abc123 (just one file: network.har). what next?
maya.k: can you also upload console.txt + curl.txt? if not, tell us whether the HAR contains response bodies (we need them).
customer_jane: HAR includes bodies. console export too attached (console-logs.txt).
aj: thanks. i'll pull request-id traces. if we see missing request-id, we'll trace to the edge logs.
leo: quick tip — if request ids are missing only for failed responses, add a small repro that logs response headers on the client and include the raw response body. that helps us detect gateway timeouts or truncated responses.
maya.k: ok team, i'll triage with infra. aj, can you check ingress logs for the time window and look for 401 spikes (1795559876-1795563450)?
aj: on it. tagging infra.
support-bot: Incident intake created: INC-2026-0316-47. assigned: eng-infra.
maya.k: customer — we'll follow up within 2 business hours. full notes attached to the incident. thanks for the quick HAR & console files, those are super helpful. :heart:
